originality.rationale: The particular sharp ℓ∞ gain limit and noncommuting finite-cycle iterated limits are not stated or implication-covered by inspected primary sources and closest published results. McElroy gives the underlying infinite-filter coefficients, Yamada describes path and cycle spectral representations, and separate published work gives range preservation or coupled-scale finite-cycle positivity; those do not evaluate the absolute-mass limit. Novelty is qualified by residual risk from older equivalent-kernel literature.
residual_risks: McElroy 2006/2008 and other older filter-formula sources might contain this special absolute-mass asymptotic under a distinct normalization or name.
Continuum fourth-order equivalent-kernel absolute integrals may have appeared in early smoothing-spline or signal-processing literature not fully indexed in the searches.
The method is restricted to standard unweighted one-dimensional lattice smoothing and fixed-cycle periodic closure; no assertion about open-end filters follows.
